scenario: AITA for letting a girl know that her boyfriend cheated on her with me? | So yes I was the side chick and didn’t know until he finally felt guilty enough to tell me. It was a one time thing, but still. Anyway, this happened a month ago but today I just now found out who she is through a mutual coworker. I messaged her just trying to look out for another girl and it completely backfired. I sent screenshots and said what happened and that she deserved better. She responded basically saying they had already discussed it and I should never contact her again, but it was really rude? Should I have not said anything? I thought I was doing the right thing because I’d want to know if my boyfriend was cheating, but now I feel dumb that I even brought it back up since she said they were over it.

Here’s why: 1. **Love Covers a Multitude of Sins (1 Peter 4:8)** - You didn’t need to expose the man’s sin to "protect" her. If he cheated, he’s already broken her trust. But since they were already over it, your message was **unnecessary and cruel**. 2. **Wisdom Over Righteousness (Proverbs 11:2)** - You thought you were doing the "right thing," but **righteousness without wisdom can cause more harm than good**. Your approach was **confrontational, not redemptive**. - **Better:** If you truly cared, you would have **prayed for her** and **avoided reopening old pain**. Even if you didn’t know her, you could have left it alone. 3. **The Fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22-23)** - Your actions lacked **gentleness, self-control, and patience**. Bringing it up again was **unnecessary and hurtful**. - You didn’t have a right to her privacy. Even if you were the "side chick," you had no authority to expose her personal betrayal. - **Your guilt wasn’t her problem.** If you felt bad, you could have **repented to God and moved on**—but dumping it on her was selfish. ### **What Should You Do Now?** 1. **Repent & Ask Forgiveness** – Pray for humility and ask God to help you handle future situations with wisdom. 2. **Don’t Contact Her Again** – She made it clear she doesn’t want to hear from you. If you see someone in danger, warn them **privately and gently**—but don’t dig up old wounds. 4. **Focus on Your Own Walk** – Instead of trying to "fix" others’ problems, **fix your own heart**.
